stem: People get hepatitis C through which exposure?

options.label: A
options.text: Hugging or shaking hands with an infected person
options.misconception: Assumes casual contact can spread a bloodborne virus.
options.explanation: Hepatitis C virus is not spread by casual contact such as hugging or shaking hands, because no blood is exchanged.

options.label: B
options.text: Contact with blood from an infected person
options.misconception: None — hepatitis C spreads through contact with an infected person's blood.
options.explanation: NIDDK states that people get hepatitis C through contact with an infected person's blood.

options.label: C
options.text: Inhaling droplets from an infected person's cough
options.misconception: Confuses a bloodborne virus with respiratory transmission.
options.explanation: Respiratory droplets spread viruses such as influenza; hepatitis C virus is bloodborne and is not transmitted by coughing.

options.label: D
options.text: Eating food prepared by an infected person
options.misconception: Confuses hepatitis C with fecal-oral hepatitis A.
options.explanation: Food prepared by an infected person spreads fecal-oral viruses such as hepatitis A, not bloodborne hepatitis C.

options.label: E
options.text: Bites from mosquitoes that fed on an infected person
options.misconception: Assumes a blood-feeding insect can carry any bloodborne virus.
options.explanation: Mosquitoes transmit arboviruses and malaria but do not transmit hepatitis C virus between people.

context: Learning objective: Hepatitis C spreads through contact with an infected person's blood.
